description:
Inconsistency surfaced during review of commit 495efcaa8 (psycopg3 migration
completion) and follow-up commit 1786150ec. The pg-family `_build_*_config`
builders disagree three ways on the fallback value used for `driver_package`
when `info` is None:

  - postgresql.py, timescaledb.py, pg_duckdb.py, pg_mooncake.py
    fall back to `"psycopg"` (bare distribution/import name).
  - cedardb.py:194 falls back to `"psycopg2-binary"` (psycopg2 pip extras
    variant - leftover from pre-psycopg3 migration; the registry metadata
    at platform_registry.py:616 already advertises `"psycopg"`, so this
    fallback string is stale).
  - questdb.py:1415 falls back to `"psycopg[binary]"` (psycopg3 with pip
    extras marker - the bracketed form is a pip-install requirement, not
    an import name).

In practice the fallback is rarely hit because PlatformRegistry.get_platform_info()
returns a populated `info` for every registered platform (all pg-family
entries in platform_registry.py advertise `driver_package: "psycopg"`), so
`info.driver_package` wins. But the divergence is a latent footgun: if
anything ever consumes driver_package as a pip-style requirement string vs.
an import-name string, the three forms behave differently. The bare name
`"psycopg"` is correct for `importlib.import_module()`; the bracketed form
is only valid for pip/uv install commands; and `"psycopg2-binary"` points
at an entirely different (legacy) distribution.

Action: pick one form (recommend bare `"psycopg"` since `driver_package` is
used elsewhere as an import target) and normalize cedardb.py and questdb.py
to match. Audit any consumer of `DatabaseConfig.driver_package` to confirm
import-name vs requirement-string usage before changing.

work_units.notes:
grep for `driver_package` references across benchbox/. Determine whether
consumers expect a pip requirement (`psycopg[binary]>=3.1`) or an import
name (`psycopg`). Known consumer: `ensure_driver_version` in
benchbox/cli/database.py passes `package_name=driver_package` through to
driver resolution; _sync_driver_options also reads it. The DatabaseConfig
field is Optional[str] with no docstring distinguishing the two.
work_units.summary: Audit consumers of DatabaseConfig.driver_package to determine intended semantics

work_units.notes:
Fixed in commit following 96ad49356. Changed
  driver_package = info.driver_package if info else "psycopg[binary]"
to
  driver_package = info.driver_package if info else "psycopg"
work_units.summary: Normalize questdb.py fallback to match pg-family convention
